name: Search-R1: Training LLMs to Reason and Leverage Search Engines with Reinforcement Learning
venue: COLM 2025 (Second Conference on Language Modeling); preprint arXiv:2503.09516 (v1 Mar 2025, v5 Aug 2025)
authors_affiliation: Bowen Jin, Zhenrui Yue, Dong Wang, Jiawei Han (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Hansi Zeng, Hamed Zamani (Center for Intelligent Information Retrieval, University of Massachusetts Amherst); Jinsung Yoon, Sercan O. Arik (Google Cloud AI Research). Lead author: Bowen Jin (UIUC).
task_domain: Open-domain question answering (general QA and multi-hop QA) treated as interleaved reasoning-and-search; search engine is used as a tool during step-wise reasoning.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent setting: a single policy LLM is trained with reinforcement learning to autonomously decide when and what to search during step-by-step reasoning, issuing multiple search queries to a real-time retrieval engine over multiple turns until it emits a final answer. Supervision is weak/outcome-only (the gold answer enables a rule-based EM reward); no per-step or trajectory-level annotation is required. The search engine is modeled as part of the environment, so rollouts interleave LLM-generated tokens with retrieved tokens. Training merges NQ and HotpotQA training sets; evaluation covers both in-domain and out-of-domain QA datasets.
what_is_retrieved: Documents/passages (top-k Wikipedia passages) returned by the search engine in response to LLM-generated natural-language search queries.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: retrieval targets a fixed 2018 Wikipedia dump as the knowledge source; there is no agent-written growing/episodic memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking: a fixed number of passages (default top-3) is retrieved per query; the system relies on multi-turn querying rather than completeness-of-set or precision-driven variable-size retrieval. The retriever itself is off-the-shelf and not optimized for completeness.
retrieval_unit: document (Wikipedia passage); the top-k retrieved passages are injected as a block enclosed in <information> and </information> tokens.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-built: a fixed prebuilt dense index over the 2018 Wikipedia dump. The retrievable store is frozen and does not grow during training or deployment.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector (dense) index over Wikipedia passages (E5 embeddings); no graph/hierarchical/cluster organization reported.
retriever_type: Dense retriever (E5) as the default search engine; the framework is retriever-agnostic and the released code also supports BM25 and online web search, but the main experiments use a frozen dense E5 retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf, frozen): the retriever (E5) is not trained or adapted; only the policy LLM is optimized by RL. The learning signal (outcome reward) flows to the LLM's query-generation and reasoning policy, not to the retriever.
query_construction: Thought-conditioned: the LLM generates a free-text search query inside <search>...</search> tokens during reasoning, conditioned on the question and prior reasoning/retrieved context. Queries are emitted autonomously by the learned policy rather than copying the raw input.
query_granularity: Step/turn-level: a separate query is constructed at each reasoning step where the model decides to search, supporting multiple queries across turns within a single rollout (multi-turn, multi-query).
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / agent-initiated: the LLM decides when to retrieve by emitting <search></search> tokens during reasoning; retrieval can occur multiple times per rollout up to a maximum action budget B.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent-initiated request: retrieval is triggered when the policy LLM generates the </search> token; the surrounding system loop detects this token, extracts the enclosed query, calls the search engine, and appends results in <information></information>. The decision is a learned behavior shaped by the outcome reward, not a fixed schedule or external confidence/uncertainty signal.
reranking: None reported; the top-k passages from the dense retriever are used directly without a separate reranking stage.
retrieved_context_refinement: None: retrieved passages are inserted verbatim into the rollout within <information></information> tokens with no decomposition, distillation, distractor filtering, or compression. Robustness is instead handled at the training-loss level via retrieved-token loss masking.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt/context augmentation as a training signal: retrieved passages are appended to the ongoing rollout sequence as additional context for subsequent generation, and the whole interleaved trajectory is optimized end-to-end by RL (PPO/GRPO) with an outcome reward. Retrieved tokens are masked out of the policy-gradient loss.
planning_integration: Inside a search loop with per-step interleaving: retrieval is woven into an iterative reason-then-(optionally)-search loop (retrieve-as-you-reason). The LLM alternates <think> reasoning, <search> query, <information> retrieved context, and finally <answer>, dynamically adjusting how many search calls to make based on problem complexity.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-reasoning-step / per-tool-call within a rollout: each search call is interleaved between reasoning steps (turns), and multiple search-call turns can occur within a single rollout.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved passages (verbatim document text) injected as natural-language context enclosed in <information></information> tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw passage/document (no distillation or abstraction into strategies, guidelines, workflows, or skills).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Retrieved-token loss masking: the policy-gradient (and KL) loss is computed only over LLM-generated tokens, masking out retrieved tokens so the model is not optimized to imitate retrieved content; this stabilizes training and improves robustness to retrieved context (ablation shows avg EM 0.431 with mask vs 0.343 without on Qwen2.5-7B-base). No explicit relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor-filtering module.
memory_type: none (static external corpus only; no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural/graph/latent memory the agent writes to).
write_back: False: the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills back into any retrievable memory; only the policy LLM weights are updated by RL.
online_growth: False: the retrievable store (Wikipedia index) is frozen and does not grow during training or deployment.
write_back_trigger: Never: there is no memory write-back mechanism.
failure_experience_usage: Outcome-reward learning, not stored experience: failed rollouts receive reward 0 (EM) and successes receive 1, and both shape the policy via RL advantage estimation, but no failed or successful trajectories are explicitly stored or retrieved as memory. Rejection-sampling baseline uses success-only trajectories, but Search-R1 itself uses outcome rewards over all sampled rollouts (success and failure) without an experience store.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no memory store; only model parameters are updated by gradient RL).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partly: the DECISION of when to search and WHAT query to issue is a learned RL policy (PPO/GRPO) embedded in the LLM, but the underlying passage-selection (retriever ranking) is a fixed top-k dense retriever that is not itself learned. So query/timing policy is learned; document ranking is fixed top-k.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A / single-agent: a single policy LLM with no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.
benchmarks: NQ (Natural Questions), TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique, Bamboogle (seven QA datasets). Knowledge corpus: 2018 Wikipedia dump; retriever: E5; top-3 passages. Training on merged NQ + HotpotQA train sets.
benchmark_family: QA (general single-hop: NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA) and multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique, Bamboogle).
baselines: Without retrieval: Direct Inference, Chain-of-Thought (CoT). With retrieval (inference-time): RAG, IRCoT, Search-o1. Fine-tuning-based: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), R1 (RL fine-tuning without search, base and instruct), and Rejection Sampling (with search engine, using the same multi-turn rollout mechanism). All baselines use the same retriever, same number of retrieved docs, same corpus, same training data, and same pretrained LLMs for fair comparison.
key_metrics: Exact Match (EM) of the final answer against gold (rule-based string match); the same EM is also the outcome reward used for RL training. Auxiliary training-dynamics metrics: response length, number of valid search calls, training reward.
headline_result: On seven QA datasets, Search-R1 improves average EM by 24% (Qwen2.5-7B) and 20% (Qwen2.5-3B) relative to RAG baselines under the same setting in v5 (the contributions/abstract also state 41% for Qwen2.5-7B in earlier versions). Concretely, Search-R1-base (PPO) reaches avg EM 0.431 on Qwen2.5-7B-base vs 0.304 for RAG; 0.303/0.325 on Qwen2.5-3B base/instruct.
ablations: (1) Retrieved-token loss masking: with mask avg EM 0.431 vs without mask 0.343 on Qwen2.5-7B-base (PPO), confirming masking drives stability/gains. (2) PPO vs GRPO: GRPO converges faster but can collapse after many steps; PPO is more stable; final rewards comparable (PPO chosen as default; e.g. 7B-base PPO 0.431 vs GRPO 0.350). (3) Base vs Instruct: instruct models converge faster and start higher, but final performance is similar after RL. (4) Response length and number of valid search calls: response length follows a decrease-then-increase-then-stabilize trend; valid search-call count grows over training as the model learns to search more. (5) Appendix studies: number of retrieved passages, GRPO group size, case studies (R1 vs Search-R1).
evaluation_decoupling: No: only end-to-end task EM is reported; intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are not reported separately (the retriever is frozen off-the-shelf).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final-answer EM). Some intermediate process behavior is analyzed descriptively in training-dynamics studies (response length, number of valid search calls) but not scored as a quality metric; reward itself is purely outcome-based.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively via training dynamics rather than as a hard cost-vs-accuracy curve: number of valid search calls increases over training (more retrieval as performance improves), and response length grows due to appended retrieved passages. PPO is favored for stability over GRPO (which converges faster but can collapse). An appendix studies the number of retrieved passages. No explicit API-dollar-cost or latency/speedup numbers reported in the main text.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k: default 3 retrieved passages per search call across all retrieval-based methods (following Lin et al. 2023); rollouts are capped by a maximum action/search budget B. An appendix ablates the number of retrieved passages.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing QA datasets; not a new benchmark). Training merges NQ + HotpotQA train sets; evaluation on test/validation splits of seven datasets with EM.
builds_on: DeepSeek-R1 / DeepSeek-R1-Zero outcome-reward RL for reasoning (Guo et al. 2025); policy-gradient RL methods PPO (Schulman et al. 2017) and GRPO (Shao et al. 2024); standard RAG (Lewis et al. 2020); dense retrieval with E5 (Wang et al. 2022) over the Karpukhin et al. 2020 Wikipedia dump; implemented on the veRL RL training framework. Positioned as a search-augmented extension of R1-Zero-style RL.
contrasts_with: Inference-time RAG (single-round retrieve-then-generate), IRCoT and ReAct (prompting-based iterative retrieval, not RL-optimized), Search-o1 (inference-time agentic search), Toolformer/SFT and rejection-sampling (supervised trajectory imitation requiring high-quality labeled or filtered trajectories), and R1 (RL reasoning without a search engine). Search-R1 differs by learning search behavior end-to-end via outcome-reward RL with retrieved-token masking, requiring no annotated search trajectories.
lineage: Group B (RAG for task-solving): an RL-trained, multi-turn, interleaved reason-and-retrieve QA agent grounded in a static external corpus; sits in the agentic-RAG / RL-for-search lineage extending DeepSeek-R1-Zero outcome-reward RL to retrieval-augmented reasoning, alongside contemporaneous works such as R1-Searcher and ReSearch.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False: the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.
tool_document_engineering: N/A: the single tool is a search engine invoked via natural-language queries; no tool/skill descriptions are indexed or engineered.
index_content_separation: N/A: no lightweight-index-then-content / progressive-disclosure separation; retrieved passages are loaded directly.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static index for the main experiments (frozen 2018 Wikipedia dump via a local retrieval server); the released code additionally supports online web search, but the paper's evaluation uses a static dense index, not a live-synchronized/MCP tool store.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A: single tool (search engine); no inter-tool dependency modeling.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no case adaptation; not CBR). Retrieved context is used verbatim and the policy adapts via RL fine-tuning rather than case revision.
